# Tactus-web: Model primitive page refresh

## Seed Findings

- ../Tactus-web/src/pages/model-primitive.js
  - Uses type = "hf_transformers" (obsolete).
  - Usage snippet calls sentiment_model({ ... }) but does not define sentiment_model as a callable; should use local classifier = Model("...").
  - Page does not teach training/evaluation/mocks story.

## Intended Outcome

Update the marketing/docs page to reflect the current Model primitive:
- modern syntax
- correct usage
- clear Model vs Agent distinction
- links to runnable examples + books

## Content Requirements

- Replace stale backend naming (hf_transformers -> current story; prefer registry-backed + training block examples)
- Show correct procedure usage:
  - local m = Model("...")
  - call and return typed output
- Add a Training + evaluation (optional) section:
  - pip install tactus[ml] or tactus[hf]
  - tactus train ... --model ...
  - tactus models evaluate ...
- Add Testing with mocks concept (high-level) and link to example(s)

## Acceptance

- No obsolete names/CLI on the page.
- Code snippets match current syntax and do not reference undefined variables.
- Page links to canonical examples + books.

## Audit Notes (2026-02-14)

- Found only one code snippet that is definitively stale:
  - ../Tactus-web/src/pages/model-primitive.js
    - MODEL_DECLARATION uses type = \"hf_transformers\" (obsolete; should not appear in public docs).
    - MODEL_USAGE calls sentiment_model({text = ...}) but there is no variable binding; should demonstrate local classifier = Model(\"...\").
    - Page currently talks about training/eval conceptually, but does not show the current single-file training syntax (Model.training) or the actual CLI commands.
- Cross-link surface:
  - ../Tactus-web/src/pages/learn-more.js links to /model-primitive/ and uses a generic lede; no stale syntax there.
  - ../Tactus-web/src/pages/agent-primitive.js already contrasts Agent vs Model; ensure the Model page uses the same language and does not contradict.

## Update Requirements (Concrete)

- Replace the MODEL_DECLARATION snippet with a registry-backed model that includes training = { ... } (Option A) and uses current naming:
  - show type = \"registry\" (runtime) + training candidates (naive bayes and/or hf_sequence_classifier)
  - show output schema and the result.output-or-result pattern
- Add an explicit, minimal CLI section:
  - pip install tactus[ml] (for naive bayes)
  - tactus train file.tac --model <name>
  - tactus models evaluate file.tac --model <name> [--candidate ...]
- Add an explicit mocks section with a small snippet (high-level) pointing to Tactus-examples for the full runnable file.

## Outline (Draft v0)

Page: ../Tactus-web/src/pages/model-primitive.js

### 1) Hero
- One line: "Stateless predictions, built in"
- Short explanation: models are for inference, not conversations

### 2) What a Model is (and isn't)
- Stateless
- Schema-first
- Versioned
- Composable
- Contrast: Agent is multi-turn + tool-using

### 3) Declare the model (code)
Use a current, runnable-looking snippet that matches canon:
- prefer registry-backed + training block (Option A)
- show input/output schemas

### 4) Use it like a function (code)
Use canonical pattern:
- local classifier = Model("imdb_nb")
- local result = classifier({text = ...})
- local out = result.output or result
- return {label=..., confidence=...}

### 5) Train + evaluate (optional)
- Keep it crisp and accurate:
  - pip install tactus[ml]
  - tactus train file.tac --model imdb_nb
  - tactus models evaluate file.tac --model imdb_nb
- Mention candidate targeting:
  - --candidate nb-tfidf uses candidate/nb-tfidf tag

### 6) Test with mocks (recommended)
- Explain: specs test your branching logic deterministically
- Link out to the Tactus-examples runnable file

### 7) Links
- Tactus-examples (trainable model example)
- Learning-Tactus (tutorial)
- Tactus-in-a-Nutshell (quick reference)
- Programming-Tactus (deep reference)

## Snippet Source

Preferred canonical source for code:
- Tactus repo: examples/47-model-naive-bayes-train.tac (trim for page)

## Additional audit notes (2026-02-14)

- ../Tactus-web/src/pages/agent-primitive.js
  - AGENT_DECLARATION snippet uses tool names as strings (tools = {"lookup_customer", "done"}); most current Tactus examples use tool variables (tools = {search, done}).
  - Update the snippet to be correct and consistent (either show variables, or show require(...) bindings).


## Implementation progress (2026-02-14)

- Opened PR in Tactus-web: https://github.com/AnthusAI/Tactus-web/pull/1
  - Refreshes src/pages/model-primitive.js to use registry-backed Model + training block syntax, correct usage snippet (Model("name") + result.output-or-result), adds train/eval + mocks sections.
  - Fixes src/pages/agent-primitive.js snippet to use tool variables rather than string tool names.
